hook: Squeezing twisted graphene changes its electrical resistance over 100 times more than ordinary metals.

summary: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene under continuous uniaxial strain showed a very large resistance response, with a gauge factor over two orders of magnitude above conventional metals. In some doping ranges the response grew in a Curie-Weiss-like way as temperature fell, hinting at nematic or fluctuating-moment physics. The origin is discussed, not established.
title: Giant elastoresistance in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene.
